results.question: According to the Enchiridion, what things are in our control?
results.actual_answer: According to the Enchiridion, the things within our power are opinion, aim, desire, aversion, and whatever affairs are our own [3]. The things beyond our power are the body, property, reputation, office, and whatever are not properly our own affairs [3].

results.question: What does Chapter 51 say are the three topics of philosophy, and which does Epictetus consider most necessary?
results.expected_evidence: Enchiridion Chapter 51, page 71: practical application, demonstrations, logic; practical application most necessary
results.actual_answer: Chapter 51 of the Enchiridion says that the three topics of philosophy are the practical application of principles, demonstrations, and a third point that gives strength and logical connection to the other two [1]. Epictetus considers the practical application of principles to be the most necessary topic in philosophy [1]. The evidence also lists a demonstration [1].
